blocks.text: Intro
detuned upright hammers out a crooked figure; overdriven bass joins; piano strings rattle, amp hum in the room
Verse 1
rough low baritone, dry amused asides, clear words; boxy drums enter at 'You turn a book', dragging slightly behind the bass

My old shoe holds the front door open.
They've put prices on the chairs.
I give my usual introduction.
Nobody knows I'm there.

You turn a book to read the back.
That one kept me up all night.
You tuck it underneath your arm.
Yes. That one. That's all right.
Chorus
cracked sung refrain, a little more insistent; loose snare buzz and bass clank; guitar spits short dissonant answers

Help yourself
If it catches your eye
I had a good time with it
While it was mine

There's a little thread left
If you see what I saw
I got carried away
You can carry it on
Verse 2
drums and bass drop out; rattling piano and close voice, guitar amp still humming; fond curiosity, no sentimental swell

There's some yellow in the needle.
There's some blue beside the chair.
You lift the canvas to the window.
I can't help following you there.

I lean across to show you
Where I thought the green would go.
You're smiling at the unfinished flower.
Oh. You see it, though.
Short refrain
bass returns with a dirty two-note throb; half-spoken, quietly delighted

Help yourself
If it catches your eye
I had a good time with it
While it was mine
Verse 3
drums stumble back into the lurch; guitar scratches between phrases; a dry chuckle in 'I always liked the underline'

Now someone's going through the records.
That sleeve was old when it was mine.
A stranger wrote their name inside it.
I always liked the underline.

You turn it over, read the titles.
A finger taps against your knee.
You're smiling at a song I loved.
That's what it used to do to me.
Instrumental
four bars; electric guitar takes the piano figure with dirty tremolo and a frayed feedback tail; drums and bass keep worrying the same pulse
Bridge
scuffed piano and buzzing bass only; voice fond, direct, matter-of-fact; leave a breath after the last line

You pass the pictures on the landing.
You don't know anybody there.
The garden's tucked beneath your arm.
I'd have pulled you up a chair.
Final chorus
whole ragged band, more rhythmic pressure; vocal catches and cracks without getting grand; last two lines delivered with a grin

Help yourself
If it catches your eye
I had a good time with it
While it was mine

There's a little thread left
If you see what I saw
I got carried away
You can carry it on
Outro
guitar picks up the piano figure once; drums cut out with a loose final hit; one blunt piano chord, amp buzz left hanging

notebook.style: Raw piano-led art rock, lurching post-punk pulse, 86 BPM. Detuned upright piano hammered into a crooked repeating figure; rattling strings, uneven hammers, hard low notes. Overdriven electric bass with pick clank and a stubborn two-note throb. Boxy kick, loose snare wires, floor-tom thumps, scrappy hi-hat; drums drag against the bass. Electric guitar spits dissonant stabs, dirty tremolo and brief feedback tails. Small band recorded live in one cramped room: mic bleed, overloaded preamps, tape compression, amp hum. Solo low male baritone, rough and intelligible, half-spoken with bitten consonants, dry chuckles and cracked sung phrases. A merry ghost enjoys its own estate sale, offering unheard asides. Wry, affectionate delivery. Refrains get more insistent; band remains unruly. Needlepoint verse drops to rattling piano and voice. No country twang, folk-pop, crooning, growling, choir, lush strings or glossy crescendo. End on a blunt piano chord with amp buzz hanging.
notebook.idea: A merry spirit follows strangers through its own estate sale, offering fond asides they cannot hear. Artifacts become invitations: I got carried away / You can carry it on.
